title: Only a step that builds makes a Choice, and a Departure is listed first

statements.says: A Choice is made only where the ticket and the spec leave more than one way open.
A point the ticket or the spec names is not open, and a part that only touches the point does not open it.
Only a step that builds makes a Choice or names a Hand check: the build, fix and the Cut.
A review that finds the change differs from the ticket has a finding, and makes no Choice.
The drift check and the Name check give Verdicts, and make no Choice.
A question the ticket tells the Session to ask a person is a Choice, and the build answers it.
A question never keeps the ticket open: Finishing closes it, with the question and the answer in the Closing note.
Where two parts that both name one point disagree, the build takes the stricter one and writes a line that starts with DEPARTS.
Finishing writes a DEPARTS line for a fault it may not fix.
The driver lists every DEPARTS line above the Choices, and the loop goes on.
The driver hands the build's DEPARTS lines to the spec review and the drift check, and each judges whether the rule held.
Where the stricter-part rule held, the drift check gives the part that lost Contradicts, so the spec stays open until a person mends it.
Where the stricter-part rule did not hold, the spec review has a finding and fixes it.
A Hand check needs one of three things no Session has: a real device, a real outside account or service, or a person's eyes on the screen or the page.
The Suite is never a Hand check, and a question is never one.
The driver hands fix the lines the build wrote, so each line is written once and the list at the end of the run shows it once.

The driver sends each kind of step its own words: the steps that build get the Choice, the Departure and the Hand check, the reviews get none of them, and Finishing gets the Departure for a fault it tells and the words that a question never keeps a ticket open.
A true clash in a spec now ends a run with the work on the Target branch and the spec open, and a person mends the spec.
The two cases that showed the faults are run again after the change Lands, three times each, and the spec that makes the change holds their pass bar.
The runs of 3 and 4 October showed every Session using the Choice it was offered.
In one run a build took a quantity of 0 that the ticket and the spec both turned down, and wrote a CHOSE line for it.
In that run the spec review backed the build's choice with a CHOSE of its own and no finding, and the drift check gave the decision Done.
That change Landed, and the only sign was three of the 33 lines at the end of the run.
A judge that may choose chooses its way out of a finding.
In a drill whose ticket said to ask the developer before it closed, one run closed the ticket and the other stopped as Blocked at Finishing, with the work built and not Landed.
The same words gave two ends in the drill, because Finishing had no word for a question.
Of three Hand checks in the full run, two were checks a Session could run: a read of the code, and the Suite.
Every step repeated the Choices and Hand checks it was handed, so 2 Choices were listed as 5.
The build departs only by the rule, so the work is sound, and the top of the list is where a person sees a Departure.
A closed list of three kinds of Hand check is something a Session can match.
Whether a Session follows the new words is shown only by a run.
Letting every step still choose, told that a Choice never goes against the ticket, was rejected, because it asks a judge to hold back and the run showed it did not.

Having a build that sees two readings stop as Blocked was rejected, because in the run one part named the point and the other only touched it, so a stop would throw away sound work for a clash that was not real.
Having a Departure stop the loop was rejected, because the build departs only by the rule, so the work is sound.
Treating a question in a ticket as Blocked at the build was rejected, because it stops the loop for a question with a safe answer, as both drill runs found.
Defining a Hand check as any check a Session cannot do with its tools was rejected, because a Session that did not try may answer that it cannot.

Having the drift check give the part that lost Done was rejected, because a spec that rules two ways on one point is a fault only a person can mend, and a closed spec keeps the clash for its next reader.
Having the driver drop repeated lines by their text was rejected, because a Choice comes back in different words at each step, so no match on text finds the repeat.
This supersedes the part of the earlier record that lets every loop Session make a Choice, and the part that has Finishing tell a fault in a CHOSE line; the rest of that record stands.
